To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DNA binding domain of the BPV-1 E1 protein is comprised of at least two distinct regions, HR1 and HR2, which together are critical for sequence specific DNA interactions and that the HR1 and HR1 regions of E1DB are similar to the DNA binding elements A and B2 in the SV40 T antigen.
the DNA binding domain of BPV-1 E1 protein consists of two hydrophilic domains, HR1 and HR2, that interact directly with origin DNA.
we identified several new mutations that disrupt E1DBD sequence-specific DNA binding, and we assigned roles for several residues in E1DBD DNA binding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of residues in the E1 DNA replication initiator that are required for origin DNA binding.
understanding the DNA binding domain of the papilloma virus E1 protein and its role in the replication of the viral genome.
the identification and functional characterization of residues in the E1 DNA recognition domain which are critical for DNA binding and origin recognition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DNA-binding region of E1 is a highly conserved region that is essential for the replication process.
the E1DBDs of BPV-1 and HPV16 bind DNA through a similar mechanism to the SV40 large T antigen.
HR1 and HR2 (or B2) make direct contacts with origin DNA and that HR3 (or B1) contacts the origin indirectly through interactions with HR1 and HR4 (or B1).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HR3 is critical for DNA binding in all three proteins, while HR1 may be critical in papillomaviruses but not in other DNA tumor viruses.
the E1DBDNA binding domain is comprised of two elements which are both required for sequence-specific DNA binding.
E1DBD HR1 and HR1 are both critical for sequence-specific binding to the papillomaviral origin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
E1DBD HR1 and HR2 are important for sequence-specific DNA binding and that E1DBDs from different papillomaviruses have conserved residues which are critical for DNA binding.
the E1DBDBD is highly tolerant of amino acid changes which disrupt DNA binding.
HR1 is a critical DNA binding element of the E1 helicase.
